html:
The Qinghai-Tibet Railway links Xining in Qinghai province to Lhasa, capital of Tibet. It is the highest railway in the world, with over 960 kilometres of track more than 4,000 metres above sea level.

The first part, from Xining to Golmud, was begun in 1958 and opened in the 1980s. The hard part, from Golmud across the high plateau to Lhasa, was built between 2001 and 2006 and opened in July 2006. It crosses the Tanggula Pass at about 5,000 metres.

Engineers had to build on permafrost, ground that is frozen all year but softens at the surface in summer. They raised the track on bridges and laid pipes to keep the ground cold. Carriages carry extra oxygen for passengers.

China presented the line as bringing growth and tourists to Tibet. Critics, including the Dalai Lama, feared it would speed Han Chinese settlement and the extraction of Tibet's minerals. The line was later extended to Shigatse.
sum: The Qinghai-Tibet Railway links Xining in Qinghai province to Lhasa, capital of Tibet. It is the highest railway in the world, with over 960 kilometres of track more than 4,000 metres above sea level.
